phrase: Researchers found that ten minutes with AI can weaken your drive to keep trying. Meanwhile, some buyers now pay extra for art made with no AI at all.
phraseAlternatives: A study says ten minutes with AI can make people give up sooner. Meanwhile, shoppers are now paying more for art with no AI involved.
AI use for a short while appears to weaken persistence, a new study found. Elsewhere, human-made art now earns a price premium over AI alternatives.
New research links brief AI use to lower persistence on hard tasks. At the same time, some art buyers pay more to know no AI touched the work.
alt: Split scene: on the left a tired person sits with a drooping meter above and an unfinished puzzle on the table beside them, while a small robot offers a shortcut arrow. On the right, a large framed artwork labeled costs more hangs above a much smaller robot-stamped artwork labeled costs less, the two sides separated by a thin vertical line.

brief.concept: A person slumps over an unfinished puzzle as a robot hand offers a shortcut, while nearby a human-made artwork fetches a taller price tag than its machine-made twin.
brief.metaphor: Giving up early on a hard task versus paying more for proof that something was made the slow, human way.

brief.composition: Two vignettes side by side, divided by a thin vertical line. Left: a person slumped at a table over an unfinished jigsaw puzzle, a robot hand entering from the edge offering a shortcut arrow, a small determination meter above it with the needle drooping. Right: two framed artworks hung on a wall, one larger bearing a human handprint seal with a tall price tag, one smaller bearing a robot seal with a short price tag.
